summary: Close to launch-ready: the tool pages are server-rendered and well structured, but two blockers remain. Shareable scan reports are indexable, and 36 DNS-lookup tool pages share most of their text. Two earlier fixes (canonicals and the sitemap host) are in and verified.

findings.title: 1,240 shareable scan reports are indexable
findings.what: Every scan creates a public `/r/{id}/` page with no noindex. 1,240 were found through internal links, each showing another company's domain and results. Related: CRAWL-10.
findings.why: Thousands of thin, near-identical pages look like scaled content to Google, and they publish data about other people's domains.
findings.fix: Send `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, follow` for `/r/:path*` in `next.config.ts` headers, keep them out of the sitemap, and expire them after 30 days.

findings.title: 36 tool pages share most of their text
findings.what: The DNS-record tools (A, AAAA, MX, TXT, CNAME and 31 more) use one intro, one how-to and one FAQ set with only the record type swapped. The crawler found 418 page pairs sharing over 60% of their main text; the content scan found 36 intros collapse to 2 distinct texts.
findings.why: Pages that differ only by a swapped name are treated as scaled or doorway content and can hold down the whole site.

evidence.detail: intro: `Look up the ${type} records for any domain…`

findings.fix: Write a specific intro, checks and FAQs for each record type in `src/data/tools/dns.ts`, or merge the rare types into one DNS lookup tool with a type selector.

findings.title: 52 canonicals pointed at the staging host
findings.what: Canonicals on tool and guide pages used `https://staging.security.example` because `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` was unset in the production build.
findings.why: Canonicals on the wrong host send ranking signals to a site that shouldn't be indexed.
findings.fix: Set the production origin in one place and use it for `metadataBase`.

fixed.summary: metadataBase now reads SITE_URL, which fails the build if missing; production env updated.
fixed.verified: re-crawl 17 Nov: 0 canonicals on the wrong host

findings.title: The sitemap listed localhost URLs
findings.why: Google ignores sitemap URLs on the wrong host, so new pages are found slowly.
findings.fix: Build sitemap URLs from the production origin.

fixed.summary: sitemap.ts uses the same SITE_URL constant as the metadata helper.
fixed.verified: re-crawl 17 Nov: all 214 URLs on https://security.example

findings.title: Unknown URLs return 200 on the first request (soft 404)
findings.what: A never-seen URL like `/tools/does-not-exist/` returns 200 with an empty page the first time, then 404 on later requests.
findings.why: Google wastes crawls on these and may index junk URLs.
findings.fix: Validate the slug at the top of `src/app/tools/[slug]/page.tsx` and call `notFound()` before anything suspends.

findings.title: 9 tool forms use placeholder text instead of labels
findings.what: The domain field on 9 tools has `placeholder="Enter domain"` and no `<label>`; errors appear only as a red border.
findings.why: Unlabelled fields hurt accessibility and leave the page without clear text about what it does; visitors who hit an error leave.
findings.fix: Add a visible `<label for>`, helper text via `aria-describedby`, and a text error with `role=alert` in the shared `DomainInput` component.

findings.title: 14 titles are longer than 60 characters
findings.what: Tool titles append “Free Online Tool” and the brand, e.g. 74 characters for the SSL checker.
findings.why: Long titles get cut off in results, often losing the brand or the key phrase.

evidence.detail: 74 chars: SSL Certificate Checker - Free Online SSL Test Tool | Example Security

findings.fix: Shorten the tool title pattern in `src/lib/seo.ts` to “{Tool} - Free {Thing} Check”.

findings.title: robots.txt blocks OAI-SearchBot and PerplexityBot
findings.what: The robots file blocks every AI crawler, including the search crawlers that decide whether the site is cited in ChatGPT and Perplexity answers.
findings.why: Blocking search crawlers keeps a free-tools brand out of AI answers; blocking only training crawlers is a common middle ground.
findings.fix: Decide the policy and record it in the SEO profile.

decision.question: Should AI search crawlers be allowed?
options: Block training crawlers only (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, CCBot)
decision.recommendation: Block training only, so the tools can still be cited in AI answers.

findings.title: No /.well-known/security.txt
findings.why: Researchers look for it first; a security company without one looks careless.
findings.fix: Publish one following RFC 9116 (template in the skill's examples/snippets.md).

decisions.question: Launch the 36 DNS tools now or after rewriting?
decisions.context: They're live in staging and linked from the tools hub.
options: Launch 6 core types now, hold the rest
decisions.recommendation: Launch the 6 most-searched types now with unique copy and hold the rest.
